nodes.name: Pulsed Laser Deposition of SrTiO3 thin films
nodes.procedure: Sr-excess and Ti-excess SrTiO3 thin films were prepared using the pulsed laser deposition (PLD) method. STEM images confirmed that the Sr vacancy cluster in both samples has a rod-type configuration.
nodes.source_text: Kobayashi et al. presented a unique strain engineering method involving SrTiO3 crystal with low and high Sr vacancy concentration regions. The group prepared Sr-excess and Ti-excess SrTiO3 thin films using the pulsed laser deposition (PLD) method.

nodes.name: Anodic dissolution growth of HKUST-1
nodes.procedure: In-situ EC-AFM to probe the initial stage of Cu HKUST-1 metal-organic framework (MOF) coating during the anodic dissolution method. Electrochemical testing identified -225mV vs Pt as the least anodic applied potential that results in the growth of the HKUST-1 coating, with the Cu2+ cations at the anode surface initiating the coating growth.

unit_operations.name: Anodic Dissolution
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Electrochemical testing identified -225mV vs Pt as the least anodic applied potential that results in the growth of the HKUST-1 coating

nodes.source_text: Worrall et al. used in-situ EC-AFM to probe the initial stage of Cu HKUST-1 metal-organic framework (MOF) coating during the anodic dissolution method.

nodes.name: NiCo sulfide-NiCo oxide supported on functionalized graphite paper (FGP) (NCS-NCO/FGPO)
NiCo sulfide-NiCo oxide supported on functionalized graphite paper (FGP) (NCS-NCO/FGPO)

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM displays obvious stacking faults and holes on the surface of NCS-NCO/FGPO representing large number of defect sites associated with low coordination from partial S to O substitution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HR-TEM displays the obvious stacking faults and holes on the surface of NiCo sulfide-NiCo oxide supported on functionalized graphite paper (FGP) (NCS-NCO/FGPO) (Fig. 1a) ... holes represent the large number of defect sites associated with the low coordination produced during the partial substitution of the S atoms by O atoms.

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM shows edge and screw dislocations on exposed planes of NiMnOx sample material.
nodes.evidence_snippet: edge and screw dislocations appeared on exposed planes of NiMnOx sample material via HR-TEM (Fig. 1b,c)

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM reveals high degree of lattice distortion in NiMoS4-12 nanoflakes correlated to crystalline-amorphous state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HR-TEM reveals a high degree of lattice distortion in the NiMoS4-12 nanoflakes (Fig. 1d,e)

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM verifies lower Sr concentration in Ti-excess SrTiO3 film with weak Sr column intensity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM verified the lower Sr concentration in Ti-excess SrTiO3 film as demonstrated by the weak Sr column intensity

nodes.characterization_summary: LAADF-STEM shows bright contrast around Sr vacancy cluster indicating strain field surrounding surface defect in SrTiO3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: bright contrast around the Sr vacancy cluster in the LAADF-STEM image (Fig. 1i) indicated the presence of a strain field

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM shows morphology and height of surface bumps of IrO2 thin films change with temperature; RMS roughness of 1.8 at 600°C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: AFM was performed to unravel the geometrical arrangement of [IrO6] octahedra in the (100)IrO2 thin film substrate ... highest RMS of 1.8 was obtained at 600°C

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of both pristine Co3O4 and V-doped Co3O4 show cubic phase; V-doped shows broadened peaks with reduced intensity and shift toward lower 2θ indicating V incorporation, decreased crystallite size, and surface defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD patterns of pristine Co3O4 and vanadium-doped Co3O4 (V-doped Co3O4) ... XRD pattern of V-doped Co3O4 displayed broadened peaks with reduced intensity ... slight shift of V-doped Co3O4 peaks toward a lower 20, implying the successful incorporation of V dopants

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Pt 4f peaks shift to lower binding energy and W 4f peaks shift to higher binding energy after 10,000 HER cycles for Pt/def-WO3@CFC indicating electron transfer to Pt and W valence change from +4 to +6 due to oxygen vacancy disappearance.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS Pt 4f and W 4f spectra of the samples. After 10,000 HER cycles, the Pt 4f7/2 and 4f5/2 peaks of Pt/def WO3@CFC shifted towards lower binding energy due to the electron transfer to Pt atoms ... W 4f7/2 and 4f5/2 peaks ... shifted to the higher binding energy ... altered the valence state of W from +4 to +6 due to the disappearance of oxygen vacancies

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS O 1s peak area at ~531.2 eV (defect sites) larger for 5% Ce-doped NiFe-LDH/CNT than pristine NiFe-LDH/CNT indicating oxygen vacancy formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: peak area of the O2 region of 5% Ce-doped NiFe-LDH/CNT was larger than that of pristine NiFe-LDH/CNT (Fig. 2d), indicating that the high and flexible coordination number of cerium ions induced the formation of oxygen vacancy and surface lattice distortion.

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR signal with g=1.97 for pristine NiFe-LDH weakened to g=1.96 for NiFe-LDH-Vo indicating decreased oxygen vacancy concentration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: signal in EPR with a Landé factor (g) of 1.97 for pristine NiFe-LDH was visibly weakened to 1.96 ... linked to the relative amount of oxygen vacancies
